RE: Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination
Member: Quinn Carter
Member ID: W142538049
Reference number: POC-698F4692AE-97118
Date of denial notice: 2026-08-12
Requested service: Total knee replacement, CPT 27447
Appeal deadline: 2027-02-08

To the Appeals Review Committee:

I am writing to formally appeal the denial of prior authorization for a total knee replacement (CPT 27447), as set forth in the Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination dated 2026-08-12, reference number POC-698F4692AE-97118. The stated reason for denial was that "the clinical records submitted do not document an adequate trial of conservative treatment prior to the requested surgery." I respectfully disagree, and I ask that the plan reconsider this determination in light of the documentation summarized below, which I believe was either not fully considered or not clearly organized in the original submission.

Policy Applied

I understand the plan's coverage decision for knee arthroplasty is governed by Aetna Clinical Policy Bulletin Number: 0660, "Knee Arthroplasty" (https://www.aetna.com/cpb/medical/data/600_699/0660.html). I was not able to independently confirm the specific effective or last-revised date of the version of CPB 0660 that was applied to my request, and I ask that Aetna identify that date and, if the criteria differ from what is quoted below, provide the exact text that was applied to my case.

Based on the copy of CPB 0660 I was able to review, the medical-necessity criteria for total knee arthroplasty state, in relevant part:

"FDA approved total knee arthroplasty (TKA) prosthesis is considered medically necessary for adult members when the following criteria are met... Member has advanced joint disease demonstrated by: Pain and functional disability that interferes with ADLs from injury due to osteoarthritis, rheumatoid arthritis, avascular necrosis, or post-traumatic arthritis of the knee joint; and Limited range of motion, crepitus, or effusion or swelling of knee joint on physical examination; and Member has any of the following: Radiographic evidence of moderate/severe osteoarthritis of knee joint (i.e., Kellgren-Lawrence Grade 3 or 4)... and History of unsuccessful conservative therapy (non-surgical medical management; 12 or 24 weeks depending on age/body mass index (BMI)) that is clearly addressed in the medical record."

The policy further specifies:

"Members with osteoarthritis, traumatic arthritis, or avascular necrosis should have at least 12 weeks of non-surgical treatment documented in the medical record (at least 24 weeks for persons with a relative contraindication) - with at least half of the necessary conservative therapy consisting of formal physical therapy (in-person with a licensed physical therapist as opposed to home or virtual physical therapy) in the past year, including all of the following, unless contraindicated: Anti-inflammatory medications or analgesics; and Flexibility and muscle strengthening exercises; and Activity modification; and Supervised physical therapy (in-person with a licensed physical therapist... ; activities of daily living (ADLs) diminished despite completing a plan of care); and Assistive device use (required for persons with relative contraindications... to joint replacement, optional for others); and Therapeutic injections into the knee (required for persons with relative contraindications... optional for others)."

CPB 0660 also states that "Relative contraindications to joint replacement include the following: morbid obesity (BMI greater than 40), age less than 50 years). Members with relative contraindications should exhaust all nonsurgical treatment options." My BMI is 29, and I am [age] years old, so I do not fall into either category listed as a relative contraindication under this policy language, and the 12-week (rather than 24-week) conservative-therapy threshold applies to my case.

How My Records Meet These Criteria

1. Duration and nature of disease: I have had 24 months of progressive knee pain unrelieved by rest, which is well in excess of the "history of unsuccessful conservative therapy" contemplated by the policy.

2. Supervised physical therapy: I completed 14 weeks (2026-03-18 to 2026-06-24) of supervised, in-person physical therapy focused on quadriceps strengthening and range of motion, totaling 20 visits, as documented in the physical therapy discharge note. This exceeds the policy's 12-week minimum and satisfies the requirement that "at least half of the necessary conservative therapy" consist of "formal physical therapy (in-person with a licensed physical therapist)."

3. Anti-inflammatory/analgesic medication: I used NSAIDs for 4 months with inadequate relief, satisfying the "anti-inflammatory medications or analgesics" element of the policy.

4. Therapeutic injection: I received a corticosteroid injection on 2026-03-28, which gave only 3 weeks of partial relief, satisfying the "therapeutic injections into the knee" element of the policy.

5. Activity modification and functional limitation: Despite the above measures, I cannot climb stairs without assistance and I wake 3-4 times nightly due to pain, demonstrating that my "activities of daily living (ADLs) [are] diminished despite completing a plan of care," as referenced in the policy.

6. Physical examination findings: My examination documents varus alignment, crepitus, and effusion, with a limited range of motion of 5 to 100 degrees, matching the policy's requirement of "limited range of motion, crepitus, or effusion or swelling of knee joint on physical examination."

7. Radiographic severity: Weight-bearing knee radiographs from 2026-07-06 show bone-on-bone apposition in the medial and patellofemoral compartments with lateral joint-space narrowing, Kellgren-Lawrence grade 4 — meeting the policy's radiographic criterion of "moderate/severe osteoarthritis of knee joint (i.e., Kellgren-Lawrence Grade 3 or 4)."

8. Absence of contraindications: I have no active joint or systemic infection, no untreated substance use, and I am a non-smoker, so none of the absolute contraindications listed in CPB 0660 (active infection, active skin infection, recent corticosteroid injection within 12 weeks of planned surgery, vascular insufficiency, or implant allergy) apply to me. I note that my corticosteroid injection was administered on 2026-03-28, which is more than 12 weeks before the planned surgery date of [surgery date], so the policy's 12-week injection-timing contraindication is likewise not implicated.

Taken together, these records document a completed, policy-consistent trial of conservative therapy — supervised physical therapy, anti-inflammatory medication, activity modification, and a therapeutic injection — alongside imaging and examination findings that meet the policy's severity thresholds. I therefore ask that Aetna reverse the denial and authorize CPT 27447 as medically necessary under CPB 0660.

Enclosures

- Physical therapy discharge note (2026-03-18 to 2026-06-24, 20 visits)
- Medication/injection records documenting NSAID trial and 2026-03-28 corticosteroid injection
- Weight-bearing knee radiograph report, 2026-07-06 (Kellgren-Lawrence grade 4)
- Physical examination notes documenting varus alignment, crepitus, effusion, and range of motion 5-100 degrees
- Letter of medical necessity from Dr. Lindqvist, orthopedic surgery
- [Any additional records the surgeon's office wishes to include]

Requested Action

I ask that Aetna conduct a full review of this appeal, including the enclosed documentation, and issue a decision reversing the denial of CPT 27447. If any additional information is needed, please contact me at [phone number] or [email address], or contact my surgeon's office at [surgeon's office phone/fax], NPI [NPI number].

I understand this appeal must be received by 2027-02-08, and I am submitting it well within that deadline. Please confirm receipt of this appeal in writing.

Thank you for your prompt attention to this matter.

Sincerely,

Quinn Carter
Member ID: W142538049

cc: Dr. Lindqvist, Orthopedic Surgery, [office address/fax]
